open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Is the token a State 1 runtime model, a field of another model, or an unmodelled scalar, and is it distinct from the Portal credential prohibited by P-01?
options: A project-scoped token entity distinct from every Portal credential
A project-scoped token value object distinct from every Portal credential
An opaque scalar supplied to operations
The Portal credential itself
open_points.default_guess: A project-scoped token value object distinct from every Portal credential

witness.initial: A caller has a Portal credential and invokes a project operation.
events: The caller supplies the Portal credential value as the token.
outcomes: The token is a distinct project capability, so supplying a Portal credential does not satisfy the requirement and P-01 remains intact.
The token is the Portal credential, so the operation succeeds but the deliverer necessarily receives a credential P-01 says it never holds.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Who mints the token, from what source facts, and what makes two token instances the same token?
options: The product backend mints it from a project identity
The caller mints it from local project configuration
An external identity service mints it from a principal and project
It is a configured shared secret with value identity
open_points.default_guess: The product backend mints it from a project identity, and its issued identifier gives it entity identity

witness.initial: Two callers operate on the same project using independently obtained token values.
events: Each caller requests or constructs a token.
Each invokes the same project operation.
outcomes: Both values denote one token because identity is derived from the project.
They are distinct issued token entities even when their project and visible facts match.
witness.observer: The authorization boundary and the callers

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Is a token bound to exactly one project, to a set of projects, to a caller across projects, or globally, and which model fact records that binding?
options: Exactly one project per token
A token contains a set of permitted projects
A caller token can be used for any project that caller may access
One service-wide token covers all projects
open_points.default_guess: Exactly one project per token, recorded by an immutable project identity

witness.initial: Projects A and B exist, and the caller has a token first used successfully on A.
events: The caller invokes an operation on B with the same token.
outcomes: The operation is unauthorized because the token is bound to A.
The operation is authorized because the token belongs to the caller or service rather than to one project.
witness.observer: The caller and project B's owner

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: What identifies the project against which the token is checked, who mints that project identity, and is the project selected explicitly or inferred from the folder, photo, placement, or publication?
options: An explicit backend-minted project identifier is passed to every operation
The confirmed source-folder association identifies the project
The photo, placement, or publication carries the project identity
The token itself selects the project
open_points.default_guess: An explicit backend-minted project identifier is passed to every operation and must match the token's project binding

witness.initial: A photo from project A is presented together with a token bound to project B.
events: The caller asks the deliverer to deliver the photo without a separate project identifier.
outcomes: The source folder or photo association selects A, so the token does not match.
The token selects B, so the photo is treated as belonging to B.
witness.observer: The caller and the owners of projects A and B

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Which of the three offered operations count as operations on a project and therefore read the token: scanning a project's folder, delivering one photo, and recording its publication?
options: All three operations require the token
Only scanning explicitly operates on a project
Scanning and delivery require it, but publication recording does not
An operation requires it only when its signature explicitly carries a project
open_points.default_guess: All three operations require and validate the token

witness.initial: A project photo has already been delivered, and its publication has not yet been recorded.
events: The caller invokes record-publication without a token.
outcomes: Recording is a project operation, so it cannot proceed without the token.
Recording concerns a publication rather than a project, so it proceeds without the token.
witness.observer: The caller and anyone reading the project's publication state

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: Does the caller supply the token separately on every operation, may the deliverer retain it between operations, or does another boundary validate it and pass only an authorization result?
options: The caller supplies it to every operation and the deliverer reads it transiently
The deliverer stores it for the project and reuses it
An external boundary validates it and the deliverer receives only authorization context
open_points.default_guess: The caller supplies it to every operation and the deliverer reads it transiently without persisting it

witness.initial: A caller successfully scans a project using a token.
events: The caller later requests delivery without sending the token again.
outcomes: Delivery fails because every operation must receive the token independently.
Delivery succeeds because the deliverer retained the token or authorization established by the scan.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: every operation on a project needs the token.
open_points.question: What lifecycle and statuses can the token have, which product action creates, rotates, revokes, or expires it, and does using it change its state?
options: Immutable reusable token with active and revoked statuses
Expiring reusable token with active, expired, and revoked statuses
Single-use token consumed by an operation
Permanent configured value with no lifecycle status
open_points.default_guess: A reusable token entity with active, expired, and revoked statuses; an external authority issues, rotates, and revokes it, while project operations only read it

witness.initial: A token has already authorized one scan of a project.
events: The issuing authority revokes the token.
The caller attempts to deliver a photo with that token.
outcomes: Revocation is token state read by each project operation, so delivery is not authorized.
The token has no modeled lifecycle or operations only require its presence, so delivery proceeds.
witness.observer: The caller and the project owner
